scope.summary: This standard specifies the material, dimensional tolerances, hardness, workmanship, finish, and testing requirements for setting anvils used for setting the raker teeth of two-men cross cut saws conforming to IS 12127 : 1987.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Certification under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). Tool manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a license to use the prestigious BIS 'Standard Mark' (ISI Mark) on the setting anvils as a certified assurance of quality, hardness, and mechanical soundness. Additionally, compliance with IS 12651 is heavily specified by public sector forestry departments, logging state-cooperatives, and tool repair workshops across India.

requirements.detail: The setting anvil must be manufactured from carbon steel castings conforming to Grade 1 or Grade 2 of IS 2703 : 1973, or carbon steel forgings conforming to Grade 1 or Grade 2 of IS 2004 : 1978.
The anvil castings or forgings must be properly cleaned and annealed to relieve internal manufacturing stresses and refine the steel grain size.
The hardness of the working face must be measured at six points spaced approximately 25 mm apart and must be not less than 370 HV (approximately 38 HRC).
The working face of the anvil must be machined or ground, and subsequently hardened. The peak of the anvil must be smoothly finished.
The anvil must be designed to be stable under heavy impact. Its base must be flat and parallel with the working face.
The anvil must be completely free from physical defects, including cracks, pits, blow holes, scales, and other imperfections. All unmachined portions must be dressed smooth.
The shape and dimensions of the anvil must conform to Fig. 1. Dimensional tolerances for all linear and angular dimensions must satisfy the very coarse class specified in IS 2102 (Part 1) : 1980.
The setting anvil must be officially designated by its name and the number of this Indian Standard as: 'Setting Anvil IS 12651'.
The structural soundness of each setting anvil must be tested by supporting the anvil on a wooden block and striking it with a hammer to audit for internal structural cracks.

To evaluate lot conformity for dimensions, workmanship, and finish, a single sampling plan with inspection level IV and an Acceptance Quality Limit (AQL) of 4 percent (per Tables 1 and 2 of IS 2500 Part 1 : 1983) must be followed.

To evaluate lot conformity for hardness and other physical requirements, a single sampling plan with inspection level II and an AQL of 4 percent (per Tables 1 and 2 of IS 2500 Part 1 : 1983) must be followed.

Any observed or calculated test or dimension value must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be identical to the specified value in the standard.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 12651 : 1989 is the national Indian Standard specification establishing technical requirements, mechanical properties, and sampling plans for setting anvils used to set the raker teeth of two-men cross cut saws. Developed under the Forestry and Plantation Machinery Sectional Committee (AFDC 64) and reaffirmed in 2024, this standard ensures the physical durability and testing reliability of the anvils used in logging maintenance yards. It mandates constructing the anvil from Grade 1 or 2 carbon steel castings (IS 2703) or forgings (IS 2004), stress-relieving via annealing, and establishing a working face hardness of not less than 370 HV (~38 HRC). It enforces strict defect controls, coarse class tolerances (IS 2102 Part 1), a wooden-block hammer strike soundness test, and detailed lot-based sampling plans (IS 2500 Part 1) with an AQL of 4% to verify commercial lot quality.
